tagline: An interstate that keeps a campground in its median.
intro: The byway leaves Puget Sound on Interstate 90, crosses Lake Washington on floating bridges and passes Issaquah under the Issaquah Alps. Past North Bend it follows the South Fork of the Snoqualmie into the Cascades. Near the Asahel Curtis picnic area the two directions part around a campground in the median, then climb on high viaducts to Snoqualmie Pass, 3,022 feet. Then it runs down the shore of Keechelus Lake and on to Cle Elum and out to the ranches at Thorp.

The pass carried a wagon road in 1867, and 400 motorists dedicated the Sunset Highway at the summit in 1915. Between Hyak and Stampede Pass the animals now have a bridge of their own over the freeway.
season: Autumn, for the fall color, by the state tourism office's advice.

moments.title: Issaquah
moments.text: A mining town that turned to timber when the mines gave out in the 1890s, at the south end of Lake Sammamish, with a salmon hatchery and the Issaquah Alps behind it.

moments.title: Keechelus Lake
moments.text: The source of the Yakima River, its name means few fish. The freeway hugs its eastern shore, where bridges replaced the old snowshed in 2014.

moments.title: Thorp
moments.text: At the narrow west end of the Kittitas Valley, where the Cascade forest gives way to cattle ranches and hay fields, the byway ends by the old Thorp Mill.

practical: Snoqualmie Pass is kept open all winter but can close for heavy snow or avalanche control, and chains are sometimes required. Check pass conditions before crossing.
